cases.note: TryParse, Dictionary.TryGetValue and ref on simple locals convert natively to existing `§A{out}`/`§A{ref}` and mutate caller storage on all four surfaces.
`out _` converts natively; `out var n` inside a conditional is kept as an inline `§CS{}` C# expression (counted as interop, effects assumed: Calor0419). #1427 decides native versus explicit refusal.
ref to an array element, a static field, and the same local twice (aliasing) convert natively and match. #1427 still owns the writable-lvalue and aliasing matrix.

Named/reordered `out`, `in`, and out-before-exception emit native modifiers, but the member fails on an unrelated empty-catch defect (X-TRYCATCH-01). Rescue paths (CLI, MCP passthroughOnError) preserve it as interop; MCP default returns isError (Calor1002, CS0161).
A by-reference call whose mutation is read later in the same expression keeps C# evaluation order.
Dictionary.TryGetValue with an int payload (a miss resets 99 to 0, so a copy would be visible) and a List<string> payload (a miss leaves null) converts natively and matches.

Generic `out T` and an `out` parameter with [NotNullWhen(true)]: the contract says these stay preserved or refused unless #1427 admits them. Rescue paths preserve `Probe`; MCP default converts natively and the compiler rejects `TryCast<str>(5, out s)` (Calor0208, isError). The attribute is carried as `[@NotNullWhen(true)]` with no flow meaning.

`Bump(ref pts[0].X)` on a struct array: the converter hoists `pts[0]` into a local copy and passes `ref _hoist001.X`. Reported native with no losses on all four surfaces; the default compile fails only on an unrelated Calor0410, and with --permissive-effects the result is 1 instead of 2. A copy masquerading as a by-reference argument.

Analysis row: by-reference mutation must invalidate pre-call nullability and contract facts and refuse or demote proofs. Not fixtured at R0; see 0.24 S1 `OBL-MUTATION-KILL` (PR #1480, undispositioned).
Analysis row: effect charging for mutation through `ref`/`out` and conservative handling of unresolved callees (#1427). Not fixtured at R0.
String targets: format specifier, alignment, escaped braces, null hole and hole evaluation order all match. Holes that contain calls compile as raw C# expressions with assumed effects (Calor0419).

FormattableString/IFormattable targets and a FormattableString-vs-object overload keep their C# target typing (the emitter re-emits `$"..."`). Default compile fails on an unrelated Calor0410 for `Kind(object)`; with --permissive-effects the behavior matches. FeatureSupport still says Full.

Custom interpolated-string handler: rescue paths preserve the handler type and `Probe`; MCP default converts the call natively, flattens the argument to STRING and fails (isError; Calor0208). Not silent, but not refused at conversion time.
Ordinary literals containing `${x}` and `{x}` stay literal (the converter escapes `\${x}`).

Native Calor: an undefined name inside `${...}` is now bound and reported (Calor0200), so the historical 'invisible to the binder' claim no longer holds; the diagnostic points at line 1, column 1, not the hole.

Native Calor: a call inside `${...}` in a function declared pure (`§E{}`) is a raw C# expression; the compiler accepts the declared effects as an assumption (Calor0419 warning) instead of checking them.

Culture: de-DE current culture through a string target and FormattableString.ToString(InvariantCulture) match. The default compile fails on an unrelated Calor0410 (the culture setter); the comparison uses --permissive-effects.
Competing overloads where target typing changes the selected method observably (string vs FormattableString vs IFormattable vs a handler), asserting the selected overload. Not fixtured at R0.
F-2 incomplete-binding counts over the corpus before and after the fix (#906 closure). Not measured at R0 (corpus not used).

The epic's `int Add(int x) => x + 1` row and a recursive local function: both members are preserved as `§CSHARP` (feature `method`), as #846 intended. Default compile then fails on Calor0410 in the caller; with --permissive-effects behavior matches. Native support is the 0.25 work.
C-1 shadowing shape: preserved as `§CSHARP`, no silent rebind (3|1002 matches). Still not native.

C-2 (shadows an inherited method), C-3 (shadows an overload), a forward call, and a delegate to a local function: all three members preserved as `§CSHARP`; behavior matches under --permissive-effects. Not native.
Outside the frozen slice: capturing, generic and iterator local functions stay preserved as `§CSHARP` on every surface; behavior matches under --permissive-effects. They must never count as native.
Analysis row: binding, effects and verification visit native local-function bodies and call edges, or refuse; no proof from omitted bodies (#847). Not fixtured at R0.

Legal iterator property and indexer: the converter emits `§YIELD`/`§YBRK` in accessors; MCP default fails Calor0209 (isError). Rescue paths (CLI, MCP passthroughOnError) preserve both classes and match, including laziness.

Disposal and exceptions: an abandoned iterator property runs its finally; an iterator indexer throws on the second MoveNext. MCP default fails Calor0209; rescue paths preserve both, and behavior matches.
Native Calor with `§YIELD` in a property accessor (the MCP output of F4-ITER-01) keeps Calor0209.
The three historical FluentValidation modules (EmptyTester, NotEmptyTester, ITestValidationContinuation) through the pinned CLI with project references. Not re-run at R0.

Historical repro unchanged on the native path: `§ARR2D{arr2d004:arr2d005:Cell}` then `§R arr2d005` gives CS0201 and CS0103 `arr2d005` (plus CS1061 on `§IDX2D ... .V`). MCP default fails (isError); rescue paths preserve both classes. The epic's 'id/name repair already exists' does not hold for this shape.

Arrays as an argument and in conditional branches: the native output does not parse (Calor0106 unknown operator `?`), so even MCP default rescues `Probe` through the parse-failure path. Rescued output matches, including no evaluation of the unselected branch.
Statement-position 1-D and 2-D arrays bound to declared locals convert natively and match.

Name collision: in `Run` the converter hoists array elements into `_hoist000`, the name of a user local in the same scope; the native output is rejected (Calor0260, immutable binding rebound). Grid's parameters match the generated `§ARR2D` id and name. Exception order is observable only on rescue paths, where it matches.

Rank and initializer matrix in expression position (jagged, rank 3, sized with initializer, implicitly typed, array nested in an initializer): MCP default fails; rescue paths preserve `Probe` and match.
No-flag `calor convert` rescue is labeled '(2 via --passthrough fallback)' although no flag was passed.
No-flag and --passthrough runs produce the same JSON loss feature (`post-validation-fallback`) and the same text; no field records which trigger fired.

Default difference: CLI `calor convert` rescues by default (RescueUnusableMembers = true); MCP `calor_convert` with default arguments does not and returns isError; MCP with passthroughOnError rescues like the CLI. No output names the path that fired or the default that applied.
Project-level `calor migrate`: defaults, rescue/passthrough precedence, member/file/project aggregation, partial failure, exit code. Not exercised at R0.
MCP `calor_migrate` (MigrateTool sets PassthroughOnError = false): outcome, provenance and partial failure. Not exercised at R0.
MCP `calor_batch`: per-file and aggregate reporting, partial batch failure, protocol error behavior. Not exercised at R0.
Library and SDK wrappers (`ConversionOptions.RescueUnusableMembers` defaults to false): documented defaults and reported provenance. Not exercised at R0.
A fully native conversion reports no interop and prints no preservation attribution.
Converter-level interop without rescue (local functions, feature `method`) is reported without a rescue or passthrough attribution.
Exit status per documented mode, `--lossy`, and rejected outcomes across CLI and MCP. Not exercised at R0.

An unrelated option changes whether rescue fires: MCP `calor_convert` with passthroughOnError and a custom moduleName does not rescue F4-ITER-01 (isError), while the same call without moduleName does. The module name becomes the namespace identity that the rescue requires to match.
Both rescue and passthrough enabled versus rescue disabled, on every surface that exposes them; precedence when both fire. Not exercised beyond F6-REPORT-02/03.
Structured DTO and envelope schema: actual-trigger provenance field or a versioned compatible extension, and wire compatibility. Not exercised at R0.

discovered.note: Outside the six families. An empty catch clause followed by a statement: the converter emits an empty `§CA` clause and the compiler parses the next sibling statement into the catch body. Native, no losses, compiles, wrong result (1 instead of 2) on all four surfaces.
